item.title: Wedding industry representatives raise funds for children's hospital at annual gala
item.description: Representatives of the Hungarian wedding industry raised around 3 million forints for the Bethesda children's hospital at the 13th Hungarian Wedding Gala.

item.title: 19 slow worms mistaken for vipers rescued from water meter chamber
item.description: A wildlife rehabilitation centre received an unusual report of venomous vipers sheltering in a water meter chamber, these however, turned out to be harmless slow worms.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands in Prague protest Czech government's public media funding plans
item.description: The crowd protested on Sunday afternoon against government plans affecting Czech public television and radio. It was the largest rally so far against the three-party government led by Prime Minister Andrej Babis.

item.title: UK: London's Santa School trains Father Christmas performers for 2026
item.description: Father Christmas is heading back to school in London. Professional Santas are learning sign language, brushing up on toy trends and preparing for the difficult questions children might ask this Christmas.

item.title: Australia and Philippines sign new defence pact amid South China Sea tensions
item.description: The Philippines is building closer military ties with Australia, Japan and the US as tensions with China continue in the South China Sea. The partnerships cover joint exercises, surveillance equipment and closer coordination between their forces.

item.title: Megaspeed says alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, left company last year
item.description: The cloud computing company with ties to Nvidia, Megaspeed, has said that Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, left the company in 2025. Huang is at the heart of an international corporate scandal and alleged to have had an affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

item.title: Mysterious object in space: Could it be a Soviet probe missing for 40 years?
item.description: The object, known as "1998 KY26", about 11 metres wide, is moving near Earth; yet something other than the Sun's or Earth's gravity seems to affect its path and speed.

item.title: "Dans Gaza" wins best documentary at Montreal's Cinemania festival
item.description: Directed by Hélène Lam Trong, "Dans Gaza" won the best documentary prize at Montreal's Cinemania festival. This 72-minute film immerses in the daily lives of four AFP Palestinian journalists, who covered the first months of the war at the risk of their lives.

item.title: Burgundy's Beaune wine auction hit as climate change halves harvest
item.description: A key event combining luxury and charity, the Hospices de Beaune wine auction is this year constrained by the meagre harvest after the summer heatwaves.

item.title: Dutch government holds weekend crisis talks to stave off collapse
item.description: Prime Minister Rob Jetten has struggled to rein in political infighting within his minority coalition, a crisis that culminated when disagreements arose over a so-called "millionaire's tax" proposed by left-wing opposition parties.

item.title: Estonian drone maker targeted in 'GRU-ordered' sabotage attempt, PM says
item.description: Prime Minister Kristen Michal said Estonia was preparing to potentially close its border with Russia to "reduce the risks to our people and national security."

item.title: Southeast Asian nations sign digital trade deal to ease payments and cut paperwork
item.description: Online shopping and digital services are growing across Southeast Asia, but businesses still face different rules in each country. ASEAN’s new agreement aims to make it easier to sell, receive payments and share data across the region.

item.title: Three commercial vessels struck by drones near Romania's black sea, PM says
item.description: Romania's Prime Minister called the attack on the three vessels Saturday 'unacceptable' and a 'violation of international law'. A day prior, a separate cargo-bound vessel was also struck. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Record immigration day in El Hierro as 1,488 arrive in Canary Islands
item.description: 12 cayucos carrying 1,235 people reached El Hierro on Saturday, and two more boats reached Gran Canaria and Tenerife. The Canaries saw 1,488 arrivals in a day and over 2,300 in two days; President Clavijo said they are overwhelmed.

item.title: Chinese electric passenger plane completes first crewed flight
item.description: The plane, a CE-25A, took off and landed in Binzhou, Shandong Province, and reportedly flew for around 60 kilometres.

item.title: Two aircraft collide at Miami International Airport
item.description: It came as travellers across the US continued to face disruption following a nationwide ground stop that caused chaos at airports this weekend.

item.title: EU forces board suspected Russian shadow fleet tanker in Mediterranean, Kallas says
item.description: The shadow fleet helps Russia get around Western sanctions on its oil industry by utilising complex ownership structures, flags of convenience and other tactics designed to mask the origin of its cargo.

item.title: Watch: SpaceX catches Starship in midair on return to launch tower
item.description: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft was successfully caught by giant mechanical arms at its Texas launch tower after a 22-hour journey, marking the first successful midair capture of a Starship returning from space.

item.title: Cape Verde heads to the polls in presidential election
item.description: Incumbent President José Maria Neves, who won the 2021 presidential election, is favoured to win a second term in office.

item.title: SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket in historic first
item.description: Crowds outside the Texas Starbase erupted into cheers as the mechanical arms closed around the spaceship for the first time, a moment SpaceX said "changed everything."

item.title: Zelenskyy questions SpaceX over reported Starshield speed restrictions
item.description: The restrictions have been directly affecting Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian jet-powered attack drones, Zelenskyy said in an address at the European Political Community summit in Dublin earlier this week.

item.title: Judo: double gold for Canada on day 2 at Zagreb Grand Prix
item.description: Canada celebrated double gold at the Zagreb Grand Prix as Jessica Klimkait and François Gauthier-Drapeau topped the podium. Georgia's Giorgi Loladze and Brazil's Nauana Silva claimed their first Grand Prix titles, while Croatia's Iva Oberan delighted the home crowd with bronze.

item.title: Hope springs eternal in award-winning photos showcasing nature’s resilience
item.description: A fragile Turkish delta and a melting Icelandic 'snow tree' are captured in the award-winning images.

item.title: Feeling the winter chill? Thermal baths and scenic outdoor saunas worth visiting in Europe
item.description: Whether it’s floating saunas in Norway or steaming thermal baths in Budapest, Europe offers travellers some spectacular spots to take on the winter chill.

item.title: Moscow says it will not dictate EU delegation's participation in Ukraine talks
item.description: Moscow, which had previously insisted that European representatives had no place at the negotiating table, has now softened its stance.

item.title: Portugal sees fresh protests over government policies seen as worsening housing crisis
item.description: Dozens of Portuguese cities saw protests Saturday against the housing shortage. Demonstrators demand rent caps, stronger tenant protection and more public housing.

item.title: France sees fifth consecutive Saturday of nationwide protests
item.description: Yellow vests, students, and education unions took to the streets to voice a range of frustrations, from rising cost of living and calls for better funding for education to stronger protection for children and teenagers and a new police law.

item.title: Canada and the Philippines conclude talks on free trade deal, Mark Carney says
item.description: "This is good news for Canadians in the agriculture sector, in the aerospace sector, even in AI, and our businesses working across forest products, mining, energy, services and beyond," Carney told reporters.

item.title: Qatar and Turkey sign defence agreement for “unified position” facing external attacks
item.description: A fast-moving reshape of the Gulf and Middle East multilateral security landscape is underway, triggered by the Iran war and the US signals that it is adapting its long-standing security presence in the region.

item.title: Armed and ready to quack: German military launches rubber ducks with assault rifles
item.description: The Bundeswehr is moving into retail: with its own online shop, the German armed forces aim to improve their public image and establish themselves as a brand. The launch range includes T-shirts, mugs and a rubber duck armed with an assault rifle – which proved so popular that it quickly sold out.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV continues trip through South America as health authorities keep watch
item.description: The huge crowds turning out to see the 71-year-old pontiff have prompted heightened fears among health authorities in Latin America, which has seen a surge in measles cases this year.

item.title: Hungary seizes millions in cash found buried in forests amid corruption investigation
item.description: Investigators uncovered large amounts of cash hidden in a variety of spots: buried in forests, concealed in agricultural buildings and warehouses, stashed inside residential properties and stored in a high-value safe in a remote location.

item.description: Putin has indicated that Russia will not back down on territorial demands to control parts of Ukraine and has rejected the idea of foreign peacekeeping troops being deployed in the country.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in China, White House says
item.description: Trump is set to depart Washington on Monday for the Philippines, where he is due to attend a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations before making his way to Shenzhen in China.

item.title: Regular coffee drinking linked to changes in gut motility and microbiome
item.description: The research team used a small electronic capsule that participants swallowed to monitor changes as it passed through the digestive system.

item.title: Russia urges IIHF to move Canada world juniors as hockey boycotts spread
item.description: Canadian authorities said Russians will be barred from the 10-nation tournament in Alberta from 26 December. Estonia, Finland and Norway plan to exclude athletes until the war in Ukraine ends.

item.title: Can Europe’s tech firms really replace Amazon, Google and Microsoft?
item.description: MEPs want public bodies to buy more European cloud services. The continent’s alternatives are growing, but they remain a fraction of the size of Amazon, Microsoft and Google.

item.title: Airlines expect to return to full schedules by Sunday night after US nationwide ground stop, FAA says
item.description: Passengers travelling to and from the US continued to face delays and cancellations to flights on Saturday despite the FAA having lifted the ground stop.

item.title: Rubik's Cube production returns to Hungary more than 50 years after invention
item.description: More than 50 years after its invention, the Rubik’s Cube is being manufactured in Hungary again, with a new automated production line launched in the country where the iconic puzzle toy was first created.

item.title: Judo: The Final Grand Prix of 2026 Kicks Off in Zagreb
item.description: The Zagreb Grand Prix welcomes over 400 judoka from more than 60 countries. Assunta Scutto claims her second Grand Prix gold of 2026, while Yang Yung Wei, Roza Gyertyas, Nurkanat Serikbayev and Shirlen Nascimento celebrate victories on an exciting opening day.

item.title: Which jobs are hardest and easiest to fill in Europe, and why?
item.description: Teachers and health workers are among the hardest to recruit in the EU, according to the OECD. Experts explain why some jobs are harder to fill than others.

item.title: COP31 is once again shying away from a fossil fuel exit but one European country is taking the leap
item.description: Transitioning away from fossil fuels appears to have become an elephant in the room as the first week of COP31 wraps up.

item.description: From the French Alps to Austria’s historic mountain towns, these destinations offer everything from challenging ski runs to snowy walks, cosy restaurants and city sightseeing – with new and upgraded rail services making the journey easier.

item.title: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': All passengers rescued after tanker collides with cruise ship in New Orleans
item.description: According to the Port of New Orleans, all 197 passengers and crew members have been accounted for. "No critical injuries have been reported," it said in a post on social media.
